title: ר' אבינא מחמרא דנהר פניא

paragraphs: Rabbi Avina ‘from the wine of Nehar Panya’—another reading, Pekod—to whom Geniva gave 400 zuz on the day he went out to execution. Rabbi Zeira told Rabbi Avina to go to his teacher Rav Huna, Gittin, chapter Ha'omer. He erred here: he thought ‘Rav Avina mechamra of Nehar Panya’ meant that Rabbi Avina came from a place called Chamra of Nehar Panya. (Siftei Yeshenim, in Sha'ar Bat Rabbim, understood likewise.) This is incorrect—could a holy mouth say this? The Gemara’s wording, Kiddushin 65b [as cited here], is: Geniva went out in a collar (to royal execution). As he went out he said, “Give 400 zuz to Rabbi Avina from the wine” (Rashi: from wine I own) “of Nehar Panya.” Rabbi Zeira said, “Let Rabbi Avina load his basket” (put his food-basket on his shoulder for the travel expenses) “and go to his teacher Rav Huna.” (Rashi: go to his teacher Rav Huna, for by his ruling and teaching he will acquire the gift without a formal acquisition.) Rav Huna said that once he says “Give,” even if no acquisition was made from him, etc. Rabbi Abba objects, etc.: “He did not say wine” (Rashi: he did not say, Give him wine worth 400 zuz); “he did not say the wine’s price” (he did not say, Give him 400 zuz from the wine’s price, requiring wine to be sold and money given); “he said from the wine” (he said to give him zuz from wine—can money be made from wine? End of Rashi). Incidentally, see how to correct the Arukh’s error under dar, third entry: “Gittin, chapter Hashole'ach Get 34, in the Gemara: Initially they would say, Let Rabbi Ravina load his basket,” etc. This is an error: it is not Hashole'ach Get, folio 34, but chapter Ha'omer 65, end of b, above.
